slice_id: F5a / P7 slice 4 / dynamic authorize_capture_set closure (follow-on to ADR-0143)
adr: ADR-0144 - dynamic authorize_capture_set closure to a genuine CAPTURED admission
proposal: Closes the authorize_capture_set -> CAPTURED gap for the dynamic P4 authority that ADR-0143's GREEN disclosed and evidence 0182's convergence_checkpoint deferred. Extends _p4_reference_bytes (new resolver parameter, closed if/elif/else, dynamic branch reuses the already-merged _p4_dynamic_reference_bytes) at all three of its call sites (_p4_checked_dispatch, resolve_p4, commit_p4_batch); extends commit_p4_batch at exactly five points (the _p4_reference_bytes call; a new per-call dynamic_reconstruction_cell local plus a single closed dispatcher _p4_close_admission_once replacing all three admission-closure call sites, which also fixes the latent _P4_CLOSE_ADMISSION(...) bug; the cas assembly, now a direct read of the frozen cell rather than a second graph read; the _P4_PREPARE call; the _P4_VERIFY_BATCH call); adds a new sibling class _DynamicCapturedAuthorizationContract (mirrors _FixedCapturedAuthorizationContract's construction, reuses the same _FixedP4Signer/_P4_BATCH_USES/_PreparedP4Batch infrastructure, no new signer or key material) whose _prepare/_verify/_verify_bytes take two additional parameters (captures, and a frozen reconstruction object) and substitute three digests already owned by ADR-0141/0142's own closed graph (root_pis_ref/dataset_g1_ref/dataset_g2_ref sha256) for the legacy contract's pea/ces/bvp-sourced fields, with no replay/evidence branch since the dynamic chain's subject_ref.kind is fixed to 'action'; extracts a new shared pure helper _dynamic_p4_reconstruct_admission_chain (behavior-preserving refactor of _dynamic_p4_close_admission's existing body) that, per the preapproval-review correction below, now has exactly ONE call site in the whole design -- inside _dynamic_p4_close_admission, itself invoked at most once per commit_p4_batch call -- with its frozen result threaded explicitly to every other consumer (the batch-signing _prepare path and commit_p4_batch's own cas assembly), never re-derived; and additively extends the already-merged _p4_dynamic_capture_admission_set with two top-level fields (consumer_document_sha256, purpose) so commit_p4_batch's shared decision-assembly tail runs completely unbranched for both resolver types. The five legacy-only symbols ADR-0143 pinned as forbidden, and _FixedCapturedAuthorizationContract itself, are not touched.
scope: Design proposal only: docs/architecture/decision-log.md (ADR-0144 corrected in place) and this evidence file. No production code, tests, or fixtures were written or edited in this call.
non_goals: Full EventEnvelope.v2 causality/ordering/provenance/correction semantics; composed-tape verification; Packet 8 durable consume-once; deployment; any edit to the fixed P4 corpus, its 500-ms clock, _FixedWormTrustedArtifactResolver, _FixedTerminalArtifactVerifier, or _p4_close_admission's v1-only grammar; reuse or extension of the fixed scope-intent/gate-evidence/scope-authorization/stage-admission apparatus for the dynamic domain; any new reserve kind, signer, or key material; a second _LifecycleAuthorizationLedger class or a subclass of _SyntheticP4CapturedAuthorizationAuthority; cross-instance run-identity checks between the legacy and dynamic authorities.
ground_truth_findings_beyond_evidence_01: _p4_reference_bytes has three call sites (_p4_checked_dispatch trust.py:2520, resolve_p4 trust.py:5305, commit_p4_batch trust.py:5324), not the one implied by the convergence checkpoint's narrative; all three needed the same fix.

_FixedCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare's blocking mechanism is two hard module-level pins to the FIXED class's own unbound methods (_P4_CHECKED_RESOLVE = _FixedWormTrustedArtifactResolver._checked_resolve, _P4_RESOLVER_LOOKUP = _FixedWormTrustedArtifactResolver._lookup), bypassing the resolver's own already-correct polymorphic resolve() entirely -- not merely 'reads resolver._records' in the abstract.

commit_p4_batch itself directly reads resolver._records inline (cas = next(...) at trust.py:5346-5347) for cas["consumer_document_sha256"]/cas["purpose"], a third choke point the prior evidence did not name.

commit_p4_batch's late pre-commit re-check calls _P4_CLOSE_ADMISSION (the legacy, fixed-only closure walk) directly instead of resolver.close_admission(...), unlike the same method's two earlier close_admission calls -- a latent bug in the already-merged ADR-0143 candidate, unreachable and undiscovered by ADR-0143's own tests because blocker 1 refuses first.

resolve_p4 independently hard-requires execution_authority_ref["kind"] in ("action","replay") with a fixed digest field name per kind, constraining this ADR's execution_authority_ref shape choice to reuse the literal existing action_execution_admission_sha256 field name rather than inventing a new one, so resolve_p4 needs no edit at all.

counted precisely, resolver.close_admission(...) is invoked three times inside commit_p4_batch's one locked critical section (not the two the preapproval reviewer's own description used as shorthand), so the originally-proposed per-invocation helper call would have re-run the dynamic reconstruction as many as four times per batch (three close_admission calls plus one _prepare call), not two; this made the fix strictly more necessary, not less.
code_changed: none; docs/architecture/decision-log.md and this evidence file only
gate: Proposal only. Independent preapproval review and owner ADR approval required before Phase 0. Phase 0 (required: this slice reaches an actually-effecting authorize_capture_set -> CAPTURED admission for the dynamic authority for the first time, crossing the same trust boundary ADR-0143's own Phase 0 scoped) must complete with zero Critical/Major before RED. No RED/GREEN, no two-final-lens review, and no merge to main have occurred.

adr0144_preapproval_review.result: 0 Critical, 1 Major, 1 Minor, 1 Nit, plus 3 claims independently verified correct and requiring no change
adr0144_preapproval_review.major: reconstruction helper determinism under the graph's mutability: the originally-proposed _dynamic_p4_reconstruct_admission_chain was called from two independent sites inside commit_p4_batch's locked critical section -- once via close_admission, once via the new _DynamicCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare -- each reading resolver._graph._records fresh. Because _DynamicP4TrustedArtifactResolver re-derives its graph view through fresh graph.snapshot()/graph.resolve() calls and has no _records slot (ADR-0143 Decision point 2), the reviewer could not verify the two reads were provably immutable relative to each other, and flagged this as a potential divergence between the bytes close_admission verified and the bytes actually signed into the batch -- the design's core safety property.
adr0144_preapproval_review.minor: execution_authority_ref's action_execution_admission_sha256 field name is reused to hold a root-capture-admission's sha256 (not an action-execution-admission's sha256) for the dynamic chain; the ADR did not call out that this reuse is deliberate or state an invariant against future kind-sensitive logic being added on that field name.
adr0144_preapproval_review.nit: the proposed purpose-uniqueness check, as originally scoped inside the (then double-called) reconstruction helper, would have run twice redundantly per batch; likely auto-resolved once the Major's fix makes the helper single-call, but the ADR did not say so explicitly.
verified_no_change_needed: claim (a) legacy fixed-authority path unaffected by the four commit_p4_batch dispatch edits + latent-bug fix -- the latent-bug fix (calling resolver.close_admission(...) instead of the legacy _P4_CLOSE_ADMISSION(...) constant directly) is correct and behavior-preserving for the fixed resolver, since its own close_admission already delegates to _P4_CLOSE_ADMISSION internally
claim (d) CAPTURED admission shape matches the legacy contract
claim (e) scope is a reasonable bounded slice, not unjustified creep
adr0144_preapproval_review.correction: ADR-0144 Decision point 6 is restructured so the reconstruction runs EXACTLY ONCE per commit_p4_batch call, structurally rather than by argument: _DynamicP4TrustedArtifactResolver.close_admission now returns the frozen _DynamicP4AdmissionReconstruction object on success (a disclosed, dynamic-resolver-only divergence from the fixed resolver's None-on-success convention -- the fixed resolver, _p4_close_admission and _P4_CLOSE_ADMISSION stay byte-identical and unedited). commit_p4_batch creates one per-call local, dynamic_reconstruction_cell = [None], and routes all three of its admission-closure checkpoints through one new closed dispatcher, _p4_close_admission_once(resolver, snapshot, admission_ref, live_projection, cell): the first call performs the real reconstruction and populates cell[0]; the second and third calls perform only a cheap, records-free _p4_snapshot_integrity fence plus an equality check against the already-frozen cell[0].expected_admission_sha256, never a new graph read. _DynamicCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare/_verify/_verify_bytes gain an explicit reconstruction parameter carrying that same frozen instance instead of independently re-deriving it, and commit_p4_batch's own cas local now reads dynamic_reconstruction_cell[0].cas directly. Decision point 7 gained an explicit invariant note: action_execution_admission_sha256 is an opaque lookup key wherever it is read (resolve_p4, _p4_entries), never kind-introspected, and no future dynamic-domain code may add kind-sensitive logic keyed on that field name without a reviewed ADR. Decision point 8 now states explicitly that the purpose-uniqueness check lives inside the (now genuinely single-call) reconstruction helper and confirms no stale two-call-site language remains. The Closed ADR-0144 construction profile section and the ADR's Status line were updated to match. Re-verified against dskit/pipeline/trust.py on this branch (no code edited): confirmed resolver.close_admission(...) is invoked exactly three times inside commit_p4_batch (trust.py:5340, 5351, and the corrected former-latent-bug line), all three inside the one RLock-held critical section, and confirmed _p4_snapshot_integrity's body (trust.py:4215-4260) performs only identity/class-pin checks and never reads resolver._records or resolver._graph._records, supporting the reuse-checkpoint design.
